solution.principle:
Related insight: Advanced constraint techniques including collider-based constraints (introduced in wasp_28) build upon the connection-configuration foundations established in wasp_15.

Related insight: Related insight: The constraints series introduced in wasp_28 and continued in wasp_15 extends further through tutorial 29 (wasp_29), which continues the constraints series with stochastic, adjacency, and connection-configuration constraint techniques. Tutorial 15 is thus an indirect prerequisite in the extended constraints sub-series.

Related insight: The constraints sub-series now extends through wasp_30, which continues after wasp_29 with orientation and adjacency constraint configurations. wasp_15 remains a foundational prerequisite for this extended constraints series (wasp_28 → wasp_29 → wasp_30).

Related insight: Related insight: The constraints sub-series now extends through wasp_31, which continues after wasp_30 with plane-constraint techniques. wasp_15 remains a foundational prerequisite for this extended constraints series (wasp_28 → wasp_29 → wasp_30 → wasp_31).

Related insight: Related insight: Smart attributes (as demonstrated in wasp_stochastic_aggregation_smart_attributes) can be layered onto the multi-part, rule-based connection configurations established in wasp_15, enabling attribute-driven constraint and selection logic within stochastic aggregation workflows. Custom mesh geometry and DisCo integration are natural extensions of the modular assembly techniques in this tutorial.

Related insight: Related insight: The foundational graph-grammar aggregation setup (wasp_graph_grammar_aggregation_setup) — defining two basic parts with directional connections and attributes, then running graph-grammar aggregation — is a simpler entry point into the graph-grammar techniques that wasp_15 builds upon with advanced constraint, adjacency, and attribute-driven logic.

Related insight: Related insight: The multi-part, connection-configuration foundations in wasp_15 are extended in advanced stochastic aggregation workflows (such as wasp_stochastic_aggregation_hierarchy) that introduce explicit part hierarchy retrieval — allowing the aggregation system to query and organize parts by hierarchical relationships alongside rule-based connection logic.

Related insight: Related insight: The complete stochastic aggregation hierarchy workflow (wasp_stochastic_aggregation_hierarchy) extends the multi-part, connection-configuration foundations of wasp_15 with attribute filtering, orientation-aware connections, part hierarchy assembly, and custom visual preview — demonstrating that wasp_15's modular assembly techniques scale into fully visual, attribute-driven hierarchical pipelines.

intents: set up wasp graph grammar rules
build discrete aggregation with grammar rules
build wasp assembly with connection rules

evolution_history.changes: wasp_15 covers connections and connection-configurations; wasp_28 extends these concepts into collider and constraint-based territory, making 'collider' and 'constraint-based' relevant tags for wasp_15 as foundational context.
wasp_29 directly continues the constraints series that wasp_15 is part of; updating context to reflect the series extends to tutorial 29.

wasp_30 further extends the constraints series that wasp_15 is a prerequisite for. The context should reflect the full chain, and orientation/adjacency tags from the later tutorials are relevant classification additions for wasp_15 as a shared conceptual ancestor.

wasp_31 extends the constraints series one step further beyond wasp_30. wasp_15 is a foundational prerequisite and its context should reflect the full chain. The plane-constraint tag from wasp_31 is added as it represents a constraint technique building on wasp_15's foundations.

The new pattern uses stochastic aggregation, multiple part types, and connection rules — all core to wasp_15 — while introducing smart-attributes, mesh geometry, and DisCo as advanced extensions of these techniques.

The new pattern establishes a foundational graph-grammar workflow that is a prerequisite concept for the advanced graph-grammar techniques present in wasp_15. Adding this lineage clarifies the learning path.

The new pattern introduces part-hierarchy as a retrievable structure in advanced stochastic aggregation; wasp_15's connection-configuration and multi-part foundations are a natural prerequisite for this concept.
The new pattern's visual preview and attribute-filtering details enrich the existing context note about hierarchy, clarifying how wasp_15's foundations extend into the full hierarchy workflow.

curriculum.title: Using the Rules from Aggregation component it is possible
curriculum.text:
Using the Rules from Aggregation component it is possible
to extract the rules sequence that created one aggregation.
This sequence can then be used in a Graph-Grammar Aggregation
process to recreate the aggregation.
When recreating the aggregation, it is possible to modify the base
part using the Transform Part component before aggregating.

curriculum.title: The Rules from Aggregation component also allow to modify
curriculum.text:
The Rules from Aggregation component also allow to modify
the generated rules sequence, by replacing the name of one
part with another one.
This allows to re-create the same aggregation using completely
different parts, having the same topology as the base parts,
but different geometry.
